description: Pure Python module providing regex-based fingerprints for detecting MCP (Model Context Protocol) JSON-RPC traffic in HTTP bodies, log lines, or packet captures. This is an intelligence artefact (detection patterns), NOT an enforcement module -- it identifies MCP traffic, does not block or mediate it. Module exposes: MCP_METHOD_PATTERNS (dict mapping method name to compiled regex), PROTOCOL_VERSION_PATTERN (regex for protocolVersion:202X), and three pure functions: detect_mcp_methods(text: str) -> list[dict] returning [{method: str, match_span: tuple[int,int]}] for each match, is_mcp_traffic(text: str) -> bool returning True if any MCP method or protocolVersion marker is found, and extract_session_indicators(text: str) -> dict returning {'methods': set[str], 'has_initialize': bool, 'has_tool_calls': bool, 'protocol_version': str|None}. Patterns are sourced from Cloudflare's 2026-04 reference architecture for shadow MCP detection via Gateway DLP -- specifically the JSON-RPC method markers: initialize, tools/call, tools/list, resources/read, resources/list, prompts/list, prompts/get, sampling/createMessage, notifications/initialized, roots/list. All regexes must tolerate whitespace variation (e.g. '"method"\s{0,5}:\s{0,5}"tools/call"'). Pure function module: NO DB writes, NO network calls, NO imports of protected modules (signal_analyser, mcp_scanner, trust_synthesiser, etc.), NO file I/O at runtime. Regexes compiled at module load. Each function must complete in under 100ms for 100KB input. Must include a self-smoke-test in an if __name__ == '__main__' block that runs the three functions against three known-good JSON-RPC MCP payloads and asserts True/non-empty results -- so `python3 mcp_traffic_fingerprints.py` exits 0 on success. Do NOT build an ingestor, scanner, or daemon; this is a library module only. Do NOT import requests, duckdb, or anything from write_service. A future directive will wire this into the scanner and/or ingestor pipelines; do not anticipate that wiring here.
